ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, on the graph of the inverse proportion function $y=\frac{2}{x}$ ($x>0$), there are points $P_1$, $P_2$, $P_3$, $P_4$ whose abscissae are 1, 2, 3, 4, respectively. Perpendiculars are drawn from these points to the $x$-axis and the $y$-axis. The areas of the shaded regions formed in the diagram from left to right are $S_1$, $S_2$, and $S_3$, respectively. What is the value of $S_1+S_2+S_3$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} After translation, as shown in the figure, \\
when $x=4$, $y=\frac{1}{2}$, \\
$\therefore$ the area of rectangle AOCB is $1\times\frac{1}{2}=\frac{1}{2}$; \\
when $x=1$, $y=2$, \\
$\therefore S_{1}+S_{2}+S_{3}+\text{Area of rectangle AOCB}=2$ \\
$\therefore S_{1}+S_{2}+S_{3}=2-\frac{1}{2}=\boxed{\frac{3}{2}}$.
